results.title: Involutions commuting with an element
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an element $t$ of a group $G$, this is the set of involutions of $G$ that commute with $t$: the elements $s \in G$ of order $2$ with $st = ts$.

results.title: Strunkov's finiteness question for simple groups (Kourovka 11.96(a))
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: This is the statement that for every natural number $n$ there is a bound $N$ such that every finite simple group $G$ containing an involution $t$ that commutes with at most $n$ involutions of $G$ (counting $t$ itself) has order at most $N$. Bounding the order expresses "only finitely many such groups up to isomorphism".

results.title: Strunkov's question on infinite simple groups (Kourovka 11.96(b))

results.title: An infinite simple group with an involution commuting with few involutions

results.title: Residue separability at a prime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$, and let $p$ be its preimage in $R$. Then $q$ is residue separable over $R$ when the residue field $\kappa(q)$ is separable over the residue field $\kappa(p)$, for the algebra structure induced by the canonical local homomorphism $R_p \to S_q$ of localizations.

results.title: Tamely ramified prime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is *tamely ramified* over $R$ when $q$ is residue separable over $R$ and the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ does not divide the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.

results.title: Wildly ramified prime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is *wildly ramified* over $R$ if it is not tamely ramified over $R$.

results.title: Residue separability, unfolded
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$, and let $p$ be its preimage in $R$. Then $q$ is residue separable over $R$ if and only if the residue field $\kappa(q)$ is separable over the residue field $\kappa(p)$, for the algebra structure induced by the canonical local homomorphism $R_p \to S_q$ of localizations.

results.title: Characterization of tame ramification
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$ if and only if $q$ is residue separable over $R$ and the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ does not divide the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.

results.title: Wild ramification is the failure of tame ramification
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$. Then $q$ is wildly ramified over $R$ if and only if $q$ is not tamely ramified over $R$.

results.title: Criterion for tame ramification
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. If $q$ is residue separable over $R$ and the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ does not divide the ramification index of $q$ over $R$, then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$.

results.title: Tame primes are residue separable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. If $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$, then $q$ is residue separable over $R$.

results.title: The residue characteristic of a tame prime does not divide its ramification index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$ with residue field $\kappa(q)$. If $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$, then the characteristic of $\kappa(q)$ does not divide the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.

results.title: Wild ramification under residue separability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ that is residue separable over $R$. Then $q$ is wildly ramified over $R$ if and only if the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa(q)$ divides the ramification index of $q$ over $R$.

results.title: Divisibility of the ramification index forces wild ramification
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $q$ a prime ideal of $S$ with residue field $\kappa(q)$. If the characteristic of $\kappa(q)$ divides the ramification index of $q$ over $R$, then $q$ is wildly ramified over $R$.

results.title: An inseparable residue field extension forces wild ramification
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra, $q$ a prime ideal of $S$ and $p$ the preimage of $q$ in $R$. If the residue field extension $\kappa(p) \to \kappa(q)$ is not separable, then $q$ is wildly ramified over $R$.

results.title: Unramified primes are residue separable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra that is essentially of finite type, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ at which $S$ is unramified over $R$, that is, the localization $S_q$ is formally unramified over $R$. Then $q$ is residue separable over $R$.

results.title: Unramified primes are tamely ramified
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra that is essentially of finite type, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ at which $S$ is unramified over $R$, that is, the localization $S_q$ is formally unramified over $R$. Then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$.

results.title: Tameness in residue characteristic zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra that is finite as an $R$-module, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$ whose residue field $\kappa(q)$ has characteristic $0$. Then $q$ is tamely ramified over $R$ if and only if $q$ is residue separable over $R$.

results.title: Correctness of counting sort
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\mathrm{key}$ assign to each record a key in $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$, and let $A$ be an array of records. The array that counting sort returns on $A$ lists its records in nondecreasing order of key, is a permutation of $A$, and is stable: for every key $q < k$, the records of the output with key $q$, read from left to right, form the same sequence as the records of $A$ with key $q$.

results.title: Running time of counting sort

results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\mathrm{key}$ assign to each record a key in $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$, and let $A$ be an array of $n$ records. results.title: Playing on a set of stacks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p$ be a position of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks, with $p_i$ tokens on stack $i$, and let $S$ be a set of stacks. The position after playing on $S$ is obtained by removing one token from each stack of $S$: its stack $i$ holds $p_i - 1$ if $i \in S$ and $p_i$ otherwise, where an empty stack of $S$ stays empty.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of natural numbers and $p$ a position on $n$ stacks. The options of $p$ in Slow$A$-Nim are the positions obtained from $p$ by choosing a nonempty set $S$ of stacks with $|S| \in A$, each holding at least one token, and removing one token from each stack of $S$.

results.title: The empty position has no options
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite set $A$ of natural numbers, the position of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks in which every stack is empty has no options.

results.title: The empty position is a P-position
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$ and every finite set $A$ of natural numbers, the position of Slow$A$-Nim $\mathrm{SN}(n, A)$ with all $n$ stacks empty is a P-position, since it has no options.

results.title: Reduced positions of Slow $A$-Nim
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A position $p$ of Slow $A$-Nim on $n$ stacks is reduced when for every stack $i$ there is a terminal position $t$ (one with no options) that is reachable from $p$ by a sequence of zero or more moves and has $t_i = 0$.

results.title: Reduction of a Slow$A$-Nim position
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of natural numbers and let $p$ be a position of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks. For each stack $i$, let $u_i(p)$ be the least height of stack $i$ over all terminal positions (positions with no moves) reachable from $p$ by a sequence of zero or more moves. The reduction of $p$ is the position $r(p)$ with $r(p)_i = p_i - u_i(p)$ for every stack $i$.

results.title: The empty position is reduced
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite set $A$ of natural numbers and every $n$, the position of Slow $A$-Nim on $n$ stacks in which every stack is empty is reduced.

results.title: The reduction never adds tokens
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite set $A$ of natural numbers, every position $p$ of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks and every stack $i$, the reduction $r(p)$ of $p$ satisfies $r(p)_i \le p_i$.

results.title: Legal move sequences in Slow A-Nim
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of natural numbers and $p$ a position of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks. A finite sequence $S_1, \dots, S_m$ of sets of stacks is legal from $p$ when it is empty, or when $S_1$ is nonempty, $|S_1| \in A$, every stack in $S_1$ holds at least one token in $p$, and $S_2, \dots, S_m$ is legal from the position obtained from $p$ by removing one token from each stack of $S_1$.

results.title: The empty move sequence is legal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite set $A$ of natural numbers and every position $p$ of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks, the empty sequence of moves is legal from $p$.

results.title: Set of P-positions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a move relation on a type of positions, where $R\,x\,y$ means that $y$ is an option of $x$. A set $P$ of positions is a set of P-positions for $R$ when no position of $P$ has an option in $P$, and every position outside $P$ has an option in $P$.

results.title: Uniqueness of the set of P-positions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a move relation on a type of positions, where $R\,x\,y$ means that $y$ is an option of $x$, and suppose that there is no infinite sequence of moves (the relation "$y$ is an option of $x$" is well-founded). If $P$ and $Q$ are both sets of P-positions for $R$, then $P = Q$.

results.title: Partial structure of the P-positions of Slow $A$-Nim
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ and let $p$ be a position of Slow $A$-Nim on $n$ stacks. If every stack height of $p$ is even, then $p$ is a P-position. If the number of stacks of $p$ with odd height lies in $A$, then $p$ is not a P-position.

results.title: Pile kept by the M-rule
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a position $x \in \mathbb{N}^{n+1}$ with piles indexed by $0, \dots, n$: if some entry of $x$ is even, the kept pile is the least index $i$ such that $x_i$ is even and $x_i \le x_j$ for every $j$ with $x_j$ even; otherwise it is the least index $i$ such that $x_j \le x_i$ for every $j$.

results.title: The M-move
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a position $x$ on $n + 1$ piles, the M-move keeps one pile, chosen by the M-rule as the first pile holding the smallest even entry if some entry of $x$ is even, and otherwise the first pile holding a largest entry. It removes one stone from every other pile, where an empty pile stays empty.

results.title: Terminal positions of exact slow $k$-NIM
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be a position of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ piles with $A = \{k\}$. Then $x$ has no options if and only if $k = 0$ or fewer than $k$ of the piles are nonempty.

results.title: Fuel-bounded length of M-rule play
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ and $f$ be natural numbers and let $x$ be a position on $k + 1$ piles. Call $x$ terminal when $k = 0$ or fewer than $k$ of its piles are nonempty. The value at $f$ and $x$ is $0$ when $f = 0$ or $x$ is terminal; otherwise it is $1$ plus the value at $f - 1$ and the position reached from $x$ by the M-move. Thus it counts the M-moves played from $x$, stopping at a terminal position or after $f$ moves.

results.title: Successor step of the truncated M-rule length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k, f \in \mathbb{N}$ and $x \in \mathbb{N}^{k+1}$, and write $M_f(x)$ for the number of M-rule steps from $x$ in Slow$\{k\}$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks, counted for at most $f$ steps. Then $M_{f+1}(x) = 0$ if $x$ has no options, and otherwise $M_{f+1}(x) = 1 + M_f(x')$, where $x'$ is the position obtained from $x$ by the M-move.

results.title: M-rule length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_k)$ be a position on $k + 1$ piles. Then $M(x)$ is the number of M-moves played from $x$ until a terminal position (one with $k = 0$ or fewer than $k$ nonempty piles) is reached, computed as the fuel-bounded length of M-rule play with fuel $x_0 + \dots + x_k$.

results.title: M-rule length of the position (3, 3, 3)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In exact slow $2$-NIM on three piles, $\mathrm{NIM}(3, 2)$, where a move removes one stone from each of exactly two nonempty piles, the M-rule length of the position $(3, 3, 3)$ is $M(3, 3, 3) = 4$.

results.title: Basic vectors of type (A0)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ and $b$ be natural numbers. A vector $z = (z_0, \dots, z_k)$ of $k + 1$ natural numbers is basic of type (A0) for $b$ when $z_0 + \dots + z_k = kb$, $z_i \le b$ for every $i$, $b$ is even, and every $z_i$ is even.

results.title: Basic vectors of type (A1)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ and $b$ be natural numbers. A vector $z = (z_0, \dots, z_k)$ of $k + 1$ natural numbers is basic of type (A1) for $b$ when $z_0 + \dots + z_k = kb$, $z_i \le b$ for every $i$, $b$ is odd, and exactly one $z_i$ is even.

results.title: Basic vectors of type (B)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ and $b$ be natural numbers. A vector $z = (z_0, \dots, z_k)$ of $k + 1$ natural numbers is basic of type (B) for $b$ when $z_0 + \dots + z_k = kb + k - 1$, $z_i < b$ for every $i$, $b$ is even, and every $z_i$ is odd. Here $kb + k - 1$ is computed in the natural numbers, so it is $0$ when $k = 0$.

results.title: Unique critical-lowering move for odd parameter (Corollary 1 (ii))
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \ge 2$, let $m$ be odd, and let $x \in \mathbb{N}^{k+1}$ be an $m$-critical position of Slow$\{k\}$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks. Then $x$ has exactly one even entry $x_i$. The position $x'$ obtained from $x$ by removing one token from every pile other than $i$ is an option of $x$, it is the only option of $x$ that is $(m - 1)$-critical, and it is the position reached from $x$ by the M-move.

results.title: Proposition 1 (odd P-positions of exact slow k-NIM)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $0 < k$ and let $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$ be Slow$A$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks with $A = \{k\}$. A position $x = (x_0, \dots, x_k)$ of $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$ all of whose entries are odd is a P-position if and only if there is a natural number $m$ such that $x_0 + \dots + x_k = km + k - 1$, $x_i < m$ for every $i$, and $m$ is even.

results.title: Theorem 2 (the M-rule realizes Smith's remoteness)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $0 < k$ and let $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$ be exact slow $k$-NIM on $k + 1$ piles, that is, Slow$A$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks with $A = \{k\}$, where a move removes one stone from each of exactly $k$ nonempty piles. For every position $x$ of $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$, the M-rule length $M(x)$ equals Smith's remoteness $R(x)$ of $x$ in $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$.

results.title: Positions supported by a (B) basic vector (Lemma 1)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \ge 1$, let $B$ be the basic-vector value on $\mathbb{N}^{k+1}$, and let $x, z \in \mathbb{N}^{k+1}$ with $z \le x$ componentwise, where $z$ is a basic vector of type (B) with parameter $B(x)$. Then $x = z$, and every option $x'$ of $x$ in Slow$\{k\}$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks (a move removes one token from each of exactly $k$ nonempty stacks) satisfies $B(x') = B(x) - 1$, where subtraction is truncated at $0$.

results.title: Basic-vector value equals Smith's remoteness (Lemma 4)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and consider Slow$\{k\}$-Nim on $k + 1$ stacks, in which a move removes one token from each of exactly $k$ nonempty stacks. For every position $x \in \mathbb{N}^{k+1}$, the basic-vector value $B(x)$ equals Smith's remoteness of $x$ in this game.

results.title: Binary encoding of natural numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bitstring encoding of $\mathbb{N}$ that writes $0$ as the empty string and a positive integer $n$ as its binary digits, least significant bit first, together with Mathlib's decoding map, which recovers $n$ from its encoding. It is a definition, not an instance; Theorem 3 installs it locally so that lists of piles are encoded as self-delimiting binary blocks.

results.title: Remoteness of exact slow k-NIM from a list of piles
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ of natural numbers of length $n$, the value is Smith's remoteness of the position $(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ of Slow$A$-Nim on $n$ stacks with $A = \{n - 1\}$, where $0 - 1 = 0$. For $n = k + 1$ this game is exact slow $k$-NIM $\mathrm{NIM}(k + 1, k)$, so $k$ is part of the input; the empty list gives the game on no stacks.
